title: Roast beetroot and fennel pasta with goat's cheese

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Every ingredient is a whole food or a plain staple such as tinned chickpeas, dried pasta, walnuts and goat's cheese, with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Beetroot, fennel, chickpeas, penne, walnuts and goat's cheese are all everyday Tesco items at normal prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a roasting tray, a pan and a sieve, and the techniques are just chopping, roasting and boiling pasta.

works.reason: Wedges of beetroot and fennel roast through in 35 minutes at 200°C, and 350g pasta with chickpeas, veg, walnuts and cheese makes a sensible amount for four, loosened with pasta water and lemon.

honest_times.reason: 25 minutes covers peeling and wedging four beetroot, two fennel and an onion plus the finishing, and the pasta cooks inside the 35-minute roast.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, penne is fairly labelled as dried pasta, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: Fennel appears three ways (roasted bulb, seeds and fronds) in a warm but light June pasta, so it is central rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling family dinner with plenty of vegetables, plus chickpeas, walnuts and cheese for protein alongside the pasta.
